newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yaohan Japan to freeze plan to open stores -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan Japan to freeze plan to open stores -- paper.

text.p: Yaohan Japan has decided to freeze a plan to open 100 new supermarkets in Japan, a Japanese business daily reported on Monday.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun said in its evening edition that Yaohan Japan, the Yaohan international retailing group's flagship firm, would also unify and downsize its overseas units as part of a restructuring plan, including the termination of its supermarket operations in Singapore and Thailand.
However, the restructuring plan will not cover its operations in China as Yaohan Japan is not directly involved in that market, the paper said.
The company also hopes to strengthen its relations with financial institutions.
The company also plans to cut interest-bearing debt of more than 100 billion yen, the paper said.
The austerity plan was decided in response to the company's falling profits and surging debt, the paper said.
Yaohan Japan said last week that it has asked its wholesalers and other suppliers to accept a longer delay before they are paid.
A Yaohan official said the company asked its 477 suppliers if it could extend the time-lag between merchandise delivery and payment to two months from the current one month.
